title: `searchAll`'s title rendering reads only the deprecated `displayNameField`, so a canonically-designated primary title never titles a ⌘K hit
body:
Filing unassigned; `domain:*` routing is the triage seat's. Found while implementing #7643 (which fixed the RECALL half of `searchAll` and deliberately left titling alone — different concern, same function).

## The defect

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, `searchAll`'s `renderTitle`, resolves a hit's title from this candidate list:

```ts
const candidates = [
    obj.displayNameField,
    'name', 'full_name', 'title', 'subject', 'label', 'company',
].filter((c) => typeof c === 'string' && hasField(c));
```

Under ADR-0079, `nameField` is the CANONICAL primary-title pointer and `displayNameField` is the deprecated alias. This list reads only the alias.

## Why it is reachable rather than theoretical

`provisionPrimary` — the ADR-0079 designation seat the SchemaRegistry runs on every object at registration (`materializeBaseLayer`, `objectql/src/registry.ts`) — writes **`nameField` only**:

```
packages/spec/src/data/display-name.ts:301   return { ...objectMeta, nameField: resolved };
packages/spec/src/data/display-name.ts:314   return { ...objectMeta, fields, nameField: 'name' };
```

It never stamps `displayNameField`. So for an object that declares `nameField` (or has one designated) and does not also carry the deprecated alias, `obj.displayNameField` is `undefined`, the entry is filtered out, and title resolution falls through to the conventional-name list.

Impact is confined to objects whose primary title is NOT one of `name` / `full_name` / `title` / `subject` / `label` / `company`. For those, a ⌘K hit falls all the way through to `return String(row.id)` — the palette shows a raw id where the object's own declared primary title exists and is populated. Objects using a conventional name are unaffected, which is why this has stayed invisible.

## The fix

Read the same precedence every other consumer of this pointer already uses — `obj.nameField ?? obj.displayNameField` — as the first candidate. Three call sites in this file already spell exactly that (the #4254 ingress gate at `assertSearchFieldsAreSearchable`, the engine's `expandSearchOnAst`, and, since #7643, `searchAll`'s own search-field resolution one screen above `renderTitle`). This would make the fourth, in the same function as the third.

Suggested test: an object declaring `nameField: 'company_name'` with no `displayNameField`, seeded with a populated `company_name`, must produce a hit whose `title` is that value rather than the record id.

## Scope note

Not fixed in PR for #7643 on purpose: that card is about RECALL (which rows come back), this is about PRESENTATION (what the returned row is called). They share a function but not a contract, and #7643's file surface was declared region-limited while another PR was open on the same file.
